I treat the Table 1 deficit sign convention as a reporting convention and express the forecast as a positive deficit in usd_billions."},{"kind":"tool","tool":"official.lookup","call":"Checked the Fiscal Data Monthly Treasury Statement Table 1 target page and release-calendar context for the July 2026 statement.","result":"The ledger expected release window is 2026-08-09 to 2026-08-17, the scheduled first-print date used here is 2026-08-12, and the prior July 2025 statement was released on 2025-08-12."},{"kind":"text","text":"Variant control: every historical anchor below is the same non-seasonally-adjusted MTS Table 1 current-month deficit concept, not receipts, outlays, refunds, or fiscal-year-to-date balance."},{"kind":"tool","tool":"official.lookup","call":"Fetched recent July current-month deficit reference class from Treasury MTS Table 1 history.","result":"July deficits used: 2021 = 302, 2022 = 211, 2023 = 221, 2024 = 244, 2025 = 291, all in usd_billions as positive deficit amounts."},{"kind":"tool","tool":"official.lookup","call":"Checked the latest available July 2025 release report and public Treasury-linked coverage for current-policy mechanisms.","result":"July 2025 deficit was about 291 versus 244 in July 2024, a 20% year-over-year increase; customs revenue in July 2025 rose 273%, or 21 billion, from a year earlier."},{"kind":"text","text":"Base rate/reference class: the outside-view base rate is the recent July MTS distribution, with 2021-2025 values of 302, 211, 221, 244, and 291; the five-year mean is 253.8 and the median is 244, but the latest two years point to a higher post-2024 level."},{"kind":"math","text":"Prior/update/interval: persistence prior is July 2025 = 291 from the same first-print Table 1 monthly-deficit variant; adjustment components are +24 for rising benefit, interest, and appropriated outlays, +11 for policy-driven deficit pressure, and -6 for tariff/customs revenue offset, giving 291 + 24 + 11 - 6 = 320. For the 80% interval, use realized dispersion of July flow levels themselves rather than historical forecast errors: sample values 302, 211, 221, 244, 291 have sigma = 41.0, so half-width is roughly 1.28*sigma = 52.5; rounding to whole billions gives 320 - 53 = 267 and 320 + 53 = 373."},{"kind":"text","text":"Counter-considerations: upside risk is a larger deficit if July benefit payments, defense/homeland spending, or net interest run hotter than expected; downside risk is stronger-than-expected tariff and income-tax collections or calendar timing that shifts payments out of July; a deficit below 267 or above 373 would land outside the interval."},{"kind":"text","text":"Review disposition: accepted the reviewer suggestions to clarify official release-date grounding and to state that the interval is based on July-level dispersion; rejected adding new FY2026 adjustment evidence because no additional fetched pre-resolution official numbers were part of the draft evidence."},{"kind":"forecast","point":320,"ciLow":267,"ciHigh":373}]}
